text:
William Wallinder waited a long time for this. Detroit's 2020 second-round pick spent last season in Grand Rapids and came into this one with zero NHL games. Sixteen games in, the 6-foot-5 Swede is playing real minutes, about 18 and a half a night lately and 20 or more in three of the last six, and Detroit Hockey Now's headline on Nov. 10 said what a lot of people were thinking: the Red Wings are getting more than expected.

He has 2 goals and 6 points, with assists in two of his last three games. The goals have come on very few chances, so that part will slow down, but the shape of his game is sound: Detroit is about even in shot attempts and expected goals with him on the ice at five on five, and he's blocked 26 shots.

History is the useful context. Of 57 defensemen taken 27th to 37th since 2005 with four-plus seasons, only 16 reached 200 NHL games, and their median first full season was 0.23 points a game. He's at 0.38. A late bloomer playing 20 minutes is a gift for Detroit.
